nodes.label: Chapter Activity Photo (children building a robot in a classroom)
nodes.rationale: Photographic, wide ~3:2 landscape. Five school-age children of varied ethnicities crowd a plywood table in a sunlit classroom: one lifts a wheeled robot chassis, one types on a laptop showing syntax-highlighted code, tablets and a parts bin on the table, wire bundles and microcontrollers scattered. Palette is warm natural daylight with primary-colour clothing accents. This is the primary proof-of-programme image for the world chapter network: it shows the actual work happening with real kids, not a stock photo of a classroom.

nodes.label: World Chapter Network
nodes.rationale: A distributed set of local student chapters, each running the same robotics-and-code curriculum with its own group of kids. The org is a network of autonomous local nodes rather than one central programme, so every chapter-facing asset has to look identical enough to read as the same movement.

nodes.label: STEM Education Program (robotics and code for students)
nodes.rationale: Hands-on robotics and programming for school-age students, taught peer-to-peer by older students. This is the concrete activity that every chapter runs, and it is the substantive reason the organisation exists beneath the global-mission framing.

nodes.label: Documentary Photography Style
nodes.rationale: Available light, shallow or moderate depth of field, honest mid-action framing, no studio backdrop and no retouching. Real rooms, real faces, visible clutter: the visual grammar of proof rather than advertising, applied consistently across the programme and event images.
